    A ratchet: every threshold sits AT the current value, so the gate fires on
    the next regression rather than on the debt already there.

    reliability_rating is D and sqale_rating is A; neither is in the gate. A
    rating condition that the project already fails would be red from the day
    it is switched on, and a gate that is red on arrival is one somebody turns
    off - which is how STP-741 happened.

    A ratchet, so every threshold sits AT the current value: the gate fires on
    the next regression, not on the existing debt. Tighten deliberately, as
    debt is paid down.

    reliability_rating is E and sqale_rating is A. Neither is in the gate:
    E cannot get worse, so a condition on it could never fail - and a
    condition that cannot fail is the exact defect STP-741 documented.

================================================================
CALIBRATION DEFECT - READ BEFORE WIRING THIS GATE INTO CI
================================================================

The sdk-js-ratchet thresholds above were derived from sdk-js-740, which
is a NARROW scan: 46 files, 6,340 ncloc, 0 vulnerabilities.

The full sdk-js codebase is sdk-js-740-full: 123 files, 16,587 ncloc,
and 36 vulnerabilities. That is 2.7x the files and 2.6x the code, and
the vulnerability count goes from 0 to 36.

So the gate as it stands is calibrated against roughly a third of the
repository. Wired to a full-repo scan it would trip "vulnerabilities
GT 0" on day one and stay red - and a permanently red gate is a gate
somebody switches off, which is worse than no gate.

This is the same failure the narrow scan already produced once as a
REPORT: "all clean" was stated on the strength of 46 files and 0 vulns,
and the full-codebase numbers contradicted it. The instrument measured
a third of the subject and the result was read as covering all of it.

Two things must be settled before this gate goes live, and neither is
mine to settle alone:

  1. SCOPE. What should the gate scan? Candidates:
       - what SHIPS (src/ plus the six plugins), or
       - the whole repository including samples/ and quickstart/.
     The 36 vulnerabilities are concentrated in the half that does not
     ship, which is exactly why the narrow scan looked clean. But the
     samples are the surface the XSS and missing-SRI findings came from
     (fixed in #62), so "does not ship" is not "does not matter".

  2. THRESHOLDS. Whichever scope is chosen, re-derive the numbers
     against THAT scope. Do not carry the sdk-js-ratchet numbers above
     forward - they belong to sdk-js-740 and to nothing else.

CORRECTION 2026-09-14. The line that stood here said sdk-net had no scope
problem - "67 files / 33,294 ncloc is the whole of that repository". That was
FALSE, and it was the same defect as sdk-js's, not an exemption from it.

sdk-net's scan follows StpSDK.sln, and the solution contained THREE projects:
StpSDK, JMSML and the tests. Samples, quickstart and plugins - 12 more
first-party projects - were outside it and therefore invisible to any
solution-based analysis. That is STP-756, fixed in sdk-net #52.

It was not academic. Nine samples did not compile at all, for two independent
reasons found while investigating: an NU1605 package downgrade and a plugin
path casing that cannot resolve off Windows. Nothing noticed, because nothing
built them.

Re-scanned 2026-09-14 with the samples in the solution:

                            before (partial)   after (full scope)
    files                        67                 149
    ncloc                        33,294             50,384
    vulnerabilities              -                  14
    bugs                         -                  28
    code_smells                  846                1,688
    duplicated_lines_density     -                  18.8
    blocker_violations           -                  24
    critical_violations          -                  78
    security_rating              -                  B
    reliability_rating           -                  E
    sqale_rating                 -                  A

sdk-js RE-SCANNED 2026-09-14, main at 9308268 plus the merges of that morning,
same local SonarQube 26.9.0 on :29000:

    files                        126        (partial scan saw 46)
    ncloc                        16,773     (partial scan saw 6,340)
    vulnerabilities              36
    bugs                         48
    code_smells                  633
    duplicated_lines_density     4.0
    blocker_violations           81
    critical_violations          28
    security_rating              B
    reliability_rating           D
    sqale_rating                 A

Those figures reproduce the full-tree numbers this file already predicted
(123 files / 16,587 ncloc / 36 / 81 / 48 / 628 / 4.0 / D / B) to within the
drift of the commits since, which is the corroboration that BOTH measurements
were sound.

Both halves of STP-740 are now derived against the scope that actually ships.
What remains is wiring the gate - and whoever does must assert it EVALUATED its
conditions, not merely that it returned OK. See STP-741.

Recorded on STP-740. The gate was demonstrated to pass AND to fail on
the local container before these objects were deleted; what is
unsettled is the scope it should judge, not whether it functions.
